facts.fact_text: On 15 September 2003, the applicants notified the Vladikavkaz Town Administration of their intention to hold a demonstration in Svoboda Square in Vladikavkaz.

The purpose of the planned demonstration in Svoboda Square was to protest against the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Regional Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (the regional internal-affairs department)'s failure to settle the social-payments debt.
On 30 September 2003, the applicants began their demonstration in Svoboda Square in front of the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Regional Government building.
About one hundred people participated in the demonstration in Svoboda Square on 30 September 2003.
The demonstrators put up tents in Svoboda Square and remained in the square day and night.
The demonstrators displayed placards and banners stating their criticisms and demands.
On 24 September 2003, the Vladikavkaz Town Administration refused to approve Svoboda Square as the venue for the applicants' demonstration.
On 24 September 2003, the Vladikavkaz Town Administration suggested that the demonstration be held in front of the Tkhapsayev theatre.

On 3 October 2003, the Vladikavkaz Town Legislature annulled the decision of 24 September 2003 at the request of the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Regional Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (the regional internal-affairs department).
The Vladikavkaz Town Legislature annulled the decision of 24 September 2003 'in connection with a risk of terrorist acts in the places of mass gatherings of people'.

The Vladikavkaz Town Legislature asked the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Regional Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (the regional internal-affairs department) to take measures to break up the demonstration in Svoboda Square.

The Vladikavkaz Town Legislature asked the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Regional Department of the Ministry of Internal Affairs (the regional internal-affairs department) to restore public order in Svoboda Square.
On 11 October 2003, the Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz declared the demonstration in Svoboda Square unlawful because it violated the rights of others.
The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz found that the demonstration hampered citizens' access to public transport and to the cinema situated in Svoboda Square.
The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz found that the demonstration hampered officials' access to the administrative buildings situated in Svoboda Square.
The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz found that the chanting of slogans by the applicants disturbed the officials' work.

The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz found that the demonstration in Svoboda Square was in breach of the Vladikavkaz Town Administration's order that all meetings and assemblies be held in front of the Tkhapsayev theatre.
The Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz found that public gatherings of unlimited duration were not authorised by Russian law.
It appears from a videotape and press articles submitted by the applicants that on 11 October 2003 the police ordered the protesters in Svoboda Square to disperse.
As the protesters refused to stop the demonstration, the police dismantled the tents the protesters had erected in Svoboda Square.
After the police dismantled the tents, the protesters put the tents back up and continued their demonstration in Svoboda Square.
On 18 November 2003, the Supreme Court of the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Republic upheld the judgment of 11 October 2003 of the Leninskiy District Court of Vladikavkaz on appeal.

On 27 November 2003, the Parliament of the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Republic decreed that Svoboda Square in Vladikavkaz was reserved for meetings, assemblies and demonstrations organised at the initiative of the authorities of the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Republic and the town of Vladikavkaz.

The Parliament of the Severnaya Osetiya-Alaniya Republic decreed that public gatherings other than those organised at the initiative of the authorities were to be held at a venue to be determined by the Vladikavkaz Town Administration.

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 (in force at the material time pursuant to Presidential Decree no. 524 of 25 May 1992) provided that organisers of an assembly were to serve a written notification on the municipal authorities no later than ten days before the planned assembly (section 2).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that the notification was to mention the purposes, type, location or itinerary of the assembly, the time of its beginning and end, the expected number of participants, and the names and addresses of the organisers (section 2).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that the municipal authority was to give its response no later than five days before the assembly (section 3).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that the municipal authority could, if necessary, suggest another venue or time for the assembly (section 3).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that an assembly could be banned if its purpose was contrary to the Constitution or threatened public order or the security of citizens (section 6).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that an assembly was to be stopped at the request of the authorities if no prior notification of the assembly had been given (section 7, case 1).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that an assembly was to be stopped at the request of the authorities if a decision banning the assembly had been issued (section 7, case 2).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that an assembly was to be stopped at the request of the authorities if the established procedure for the conduct of public assemblies had been breached (section 7, case 3).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that an assembly was to be stopped at the request of the authorities if there was a danger to citizens' life or health (section 7, case 4).

The Decree of the Presidium of the USSR Supreme Council no. 9306-XI of 28 July 1988 provided that an assembly was to be stopped at the request of the authorities if the public order was breached (section 7, case 5).
